analysis: Examined three changed files. (1) docs/reference/model-registry-format.md adds a documentation-only 'Flint local package exception' section (head lines 395-403). It describes native architecture identity `flint`, shard-only local discovery with a 1,048,576-byte bounded nonempty regular config, a strict complete weight inventory, native KV precision, and no catalog publication from local discovery. It changes no code or controls and claims no registry or serving activation. The described bounded config read and strict inventory are consistent with the existing weight-integrity expectations (T-012, T-027). Whether the code matches these claims (ModelScanner.isMLXModel, boundedModelConfiguration, FlintCheckpoint) is outside the supplied evidence. A shard-only discovery path with no synthetic index, if implemented, would lack the index-file integrity entry in the aggregate hash. That is a source-level question for whoever reviews the code PR, not a finding here. (2) fixtures/prompt-contract/v1/contract_vectors.json (head lines 25, 31-32) moves the previous expected_prompt_contract_id into a new legacy_v8 field and sets a new current ID. This is a prompt-contract version bump with the old ID retained as legacy. The coordinator-authored cacheSalt derives from the prompt-contract ID (T-041). A bump therefore invalidates and partitions cache scopes rather than weakening account isolation. Whether legacy IDs are still accepted for routing or cache reuse depends on code not supplied. (3) fixtures/prompt-contract/v1/production_vectors.json is a patch-only unit with a truncated excerpt (unit :0 has no text). It shows prompt_contract_id values being regenerated, for example 6bb9fb05... to 8171fec3.... This is consistent with the bump. Consistency with the Go and Swift prompt-contract implementations could not be verified. Remaining integration question: the corresponding implementation changes (prompt-contract version, Flint engine, scanner) are not in this batch. Provider and coordinator must agree on the new contract ID, or cache routing is lost and routing and eligibility mismatches arise (availability, not confidentiality). No security regression is identifiable from the supplied evidence.
